company_description: Paramount Skydance Corporation operates as a media and entertainment company worldwide. It operates in three segments: Studios, Direct-to-Consumer, and TV Media. The company operates CBS Television Network, a domestic broadcast television network; CBS Stations, a television station; international free-to-air networks comprising Network 10, Channel 5, Telefe, and Chilevision; and domestic premium and basic cable networks, such as Nickelodeon, MTV, CMT, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount+ with SHOWTIME, Paramount Network, The Smithsonian Channel, BET Media Group, CBS Sports Network, and international extensions of these brands. It also provides domestic and international television studio operations, including CBS Studios, Paramount Television Studios, and Showtime; CBS Media Ventures, which produces and distributes first-run syndicated programming; and digital properties consist of CBS News and CBS Sports HQ. In addition, the company offers a portfolio of domestic and international pay and free streaming services, including Paramount+, Pluto TV, and BET+. risks.title: Uncertainty regarding Warner Bros. acquisition
risks.summary: The tender offer for Warner Bros. faces significant regulatory and competitive hurdles, with a high risk of failure despite strengthened conditions and financing commitments.
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K with multiple recent amendments (February 2026) and personal guarantee from Lawrence Ellison. Language intensified around closing conditions, rising costs, and risk of non-completion. Major exposure in case of transaction failure.

risks.title: Dependence on the Ellison family
risks.summary: The company is controlled by the Ellison family, concentrating strategic decision-making and exposing it to corporate governance risks.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 1 and Item 7 of the 10-K, the Ellison family holds de facto control through National Amusements, Inc. Language asserting near-total control, reinforced by Lawrence Ellison's personal guarantee for Warner Bros. financing. Existential risk in case of strategic divergence.

risks.title: Post-merger integration complexity
risks.summary: The integration of Paramount Global and Skydance Media under a new accounting framework creates risks related to operational, financial, and systems alignment.
risks.score_rationale: Present in Item 1A of the 10-K with application of pushdown accounting since August 7, 2025. Explicit mention of non-comparability of financial results. Moderate intensity but sensitive context for a recent merger combining Paramount Global and Skydance Media.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and data protection
risks.summary: The company acknowledges major risks related to cyberattacks, business continuity, and protection of personal data from users of its platforms.
risks.score_rationale: First risk listed in Item 1A of the 10-K, ahead of financial matters. Strategic placement in the document indicating management priority. Language acknowledging significant vulnerabilities related to cyberattacks and personal data protection.

risks.title: Risk of contractual breaches post-transaction
risks.summary: Potential failure to obtain required contractual consents after the merger could lead to disruptions with certain partners or counterparties to key contracts.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified following the Transactions of August 7, 2025. Certain contracts may require third-party consents or include change of control clauses. Moderate warning language but post-merger context increases relative vulnerability.

risks.title: Potential dilution from PIPE warrants
risks.summary: The transaction's financing structure could include optional instruments leading to potential dilution for existing shareholders.
risks.score_rationale: Implicitly mentioned in the context of the Skydance transaction financing structure. Factual risk but dependent on optional exercise and stock performance. Low weighting as the risk is conditional.
